acceptance_checks: A fresh install writes a stamp naming the platform commit, the timestamp, and a per-path content digest.
doctor reports no drift on an untouched fresh install.
Editing one shipped file makes doctor report drift naming that exact path.
An absent stamp is a distinct doctor finding, never a pass.
A stamp naming a platform commit that is not an ancestor of the running platform HEAD is reported, not silently accepted.
doctor --strict fails on drift and on an absent stamp.
doctor never writes to the target.
shiki migrate --target pointing at a different repository either resolves that repository's own registry or refuses with a message naming the correct command — asserted directly.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Touching any file outside the declared locks
scope:
Write an install stamp into the target — a small JSON record naming the platform commit the install came from, the install timestamp, and a content digest per shipped path — and refresh it on every install and upgrade. It is target state, not a contract, so it belongs with the other target-owned records and must never be overwritten by a later install with older content.

Teach `shiki doctor` to report drift from it: a shipped path whose current content differs from the stamped digest (the target was hand-edited or half-upgraded), a stamp naming a platform commit that is not an ancestor of the running platform's HEAD (the target is ahead, or from a different lineage), and an absent stamp (a target installed before stamps existed — reported as a distinct finding, never as a pass). Drift must be a real doctor finding with its own id, so `--strict` fails on it.

Fix the migration target confusion: `shiki migrate` with `--target <other repo>` currently runs the PLATFORM's registry against the TARGET's state file, so it can write migration ids the target's own validator rejects, producing a permanently red required check. Either resolve the registry from the target's own `scripts/` when `--target` names a different repository, or refuse `--target` with a message telling the operator to run the target's own CLI. Refusing is acceptable and is the safer default; whichever is chosen must be covered by a test.

Add `tests/test_install_version_drift.py`: a fresh install writes a stamp; doctor reports no drift; editing one shipped file makes doctor report drift naming that path; removing the stamp produces the distinct absent-stamp finding, never a pass; `--strict` fails on drift; a stamp from a newer platform commit is reported rather than silently accepted; and `shiki migrate --target <other>` either uses the target's registry or refuses, asserted directly.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes, and what to change to get the same result.
  Symptom: you cannot tell an old target from a current one. A uniformly-old target is internally consistent, so `validate_shiki` passes and `doctor` reports zero failures — the same output a current target gives.
  Measured: `'VERSION' in TEMPLATE_PATHS` -> False; no Python file reads `VERSION` (only `.github/workflows/release.yml` mentions it); `shiki status` emits only `claude_command, codex_skill, command, config, root`; `shiki preflight` checks git-repo, GitHub-origin and `.shiki/repo.json` only; `shiki doctor` has no version check. The only instrument available today is diffing `TEMPLATE_PATHS` by hand against the platform.
  Second defect: the global `shiki` is a symlink into the platform checkout and `bin/shiki` execs the platform's `scripts/shiki.py`, so `shiki migrate --target <old target>` builds the registry from the PLATFORM and applies it to the TARGET's state file. `docs/releasing.md:145-149` shows the migrate commands with no `--target` at all, which is the only safe form.
  Reproducible when: doctor names the exact drifted paths in a hand-edited target, reports an absent stamp as its own finding, and `--strict` fails on both.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_doctor.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_init.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Give a target a version stamp and detect drift against it
